Grace: heads up — noticing a spike in traces for payment-service where DB client spans are totally missing since the router v2 canary at ~15:03 UTC. root span and cache spans exist but no sql/pg spans.
Oliver: saw it too. looks like only requests proxied through router v2 are affected. sample trace id: 0af3c9b2a7e4d1f3 — can paste a few.
Priya: can you paste the raw request headers that hit payment-service? thinking traceparent/tracestate might be getting dropped or moved.
Grace: here are two successive requests captured at the router ingress and at the backend:
```
# ingress -> router forward
:method: POST
:authority: router.internal
traceparent: 00-0af3c9b2a7e4d1f3b9c4f6d2e1a0b3c4-01-01
tracestate: vendor1=abc,oth=def
user-agent: curl/7.86.0

# router -> payment-service (observed)
:method: POST
:authority: payment.internal
user-agent: curl/7.86.0
# NOTE: traceparent/tracestate MISSING here; router added some trailers
```
Oliver: interesting — router logs show an `http2-trailers` optimization enabled in v2. It was supposed to move some large headers to trailers, maybe OTel headers got swept up.
Theo: correct. v2 introduced a filter to convert chosen headers to trailers for http/2 -> http/1 upstream paths. I think traceparent got classified as "large" and moved to trailers, but our HTTP/1 upstream client doesn't read trailers by default. so backend never sees the trace context.
Priya: that matches why we still have root span (created at ingress) but client library doesn't join the trace on DB calls since it never received traceparent.
Oliver: query I ran: `service:router AND attributes.http2_trailers:true AND not attributes.traceparent_present` — lots of hits starting at 1867501000.
Grace: mitigation options: temporarily disable header->trailer conversion for `traceparent`/`tracestate` or disable the optimization entirely for the canary fleet.
deploy-bot: deploy canary rollback requested: router-service v2.1.3 -> rollback to v2.1.2 in us-east-1. Started at 2026-03-20T15:07:02Z.
Grace: rolled back the canary in us-east, switching more traffic off v2.1.3.
Oliver: after rollback I can already see DB spans re-appearing in newly sampled traces. Looks resolved for canary region.
Theo: root cause = header_to_trailer filter + conservative header classification. Fix: ensure `traceparent` and `tracestate` are on the preserve list; do NOT move them to trailers. I'll open PR to update filter config and add explicit deny to move OTel headers.
Priya: also let's add an automated telemetry integration test in CI that asserts a downstream `db.*` span is present for an end-to-end request through the router. filed INF-1123 for that and added a short-term runbook: rollback router canary if >1% of traces for a path lose DB spans in 10m window.
Grace: adding to postmortem notes: watchlist for future router optimizations: any header-to-trailer behavior must be verified for trace context. :white_check_mark:
Theo: will follow up with PR and a config test. thanks all.
